name: Sterling-Nakamura Diplomatic Secure Container DSC-5
description: A briefcase-sized secure container with integrated biometric lock, tamper detection, and thermite self-destruct system. The DSC-5 is designed to transport classified documents, data storage devices, or biological samples with absolute security — any unauthorized opening attempt triggers an internal thermite charge that incinerates the contents at 2,500°C in under 3 seconds. The container's walls are lined with Faraday cage mesh to prevent electromagnetic scanning of contents, and its biometric lock requires fingerprint, voiceprint, and neural interface verification. Sterling-Nakamura issues them to diplomatic staff and high-priority courier services.
story_hooks: A DSC-5 self-destruct was triggered during a routine customs inspection — the inspector's unauthorized biometric scan activated the tamper detection, incinerating contents that someone very much wanted to know about.

A DSC-5 has been modified to allow remote triggering of the thermite charge — it has been given to a courier as a concealed incendiary device that will destroy whatever room they are in when activated.

physical_description.visual_profile: A compact, military-grade briefcase with aggressive angular lines and zero aesthetic compromise. The DSC-5 presents as a hard-shell executive container designed by someone who prioritizes function over form — it has the intimidating presence of a device that destroys its own contents rather than surrender them.
physical_description.dimensions: 30×20×10 cm (briefcase-sized, fits under one arm or in a vehicle's overhead compartment)
physical_description.weight_description: 4.5 kg — handheld but notably dense; requires a carrying strap or two-handed grip for extended periods
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced carbon-fiber composite shell with internal Faraday cage mesh lining
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal-gray with brushed composite surface; intentionally non-reflective to resist identification scanning. Seams and edge joints are welded and sealed with micro-etched verification patterns.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with black anodized aluminum corner reinforcements. Subtle Sterling-Nakamura logo in matte silver at center of lid. Biometric sensor array glows faint blue when active.
physical_description.interface_elements: Fingerprint scanner (right side), voice authentication grille (top left), neural interface contact pad (inset beneath lid handle). Status LED array (blue = armed, red = tamper alert, amber = low battery). Subtle pressure-release valve vents on bottom. No external keypad or mechanical locks.
distinctive_features: Recessed biometric sensor array that sits flush with the case to prevent physical tampering
Hairline LED indicator that pulses in rhythm with remaining battery life
Reinforced aluminum corner guards with stress-fracture detection etched into the material
Interior release mechanism (visible only when lid is open) that hints at the thermite cartridge chamber below the contents tray
Faraday mesh pattern subtly visible along interior seams in reflected light
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Sterling-Nakamura logo (lowercase 's-n' interlock) etched in matte silver center-lid. Regulatory stamps: GLMZ-SEC-COMPLIANCE, DIPLOMATIC USE ONLY (small red accent text), and a batch serial number on the bottom rear. No bright logos or branding — discretion is the point.
physical_description.condition_typical: In active use, the biometric sensor glows softly blue and the case is warm to the touch from passive battery drain. Courier units often show minor cosmetic scuffs on corner guards but zero visible damage to the seal. The case is perpetually locked and opens only for authorized users.
